title: Ten slots, ten keys: room for all?
hook: The table has a slot for every key. Does each key get its own?

knows: that a hash table picks a slot for each key (hash-bucket-pileup)
doesNotKnow: that the hash rule itself can cause pileups when keys share a pattern

misconception: Any hash function spreads keys evenly; only the table size matters.
objective: The learner can explain that with slot = key mod 10 the keys 10, 20, ..., 100 all land in slot 0 because they share a pattern, that the same keys spread over 7 slots under mod 7, and that a pileup makes lookups walk one long list.

claims.text: Every multiple of 10 leaves remainder 0 when divided by 10, so with slot = key mod 10 the keys 10, 20, ..., 100 all land in slot 0 and 9 slots stay empty. Finding the last key means walking the whole list: 10 steps for key 100.
claims.source: Arithmetic; Demo.tsx usedSlots(KEYS, 10) = 1, builder checked in Node (remainders all 0).

claims.text: Under slot = key mod 7 the same 10 keys use 7 slots; remainders are only 0 to 6, so slots 7 to 9 stay empty. Finding the last key takes 2 steps (key 100 sits second in its list).
claims.source: Remainders 3, 6, 2, 5, 1, 4, 0, 3, 6, 2 (builder ran in Node): 7 distinct. Slots 7-9 can never be used under mod 7 (drawn faded).

claims.text: Keys that land in the same slot are kept as a list in that slot, and finding one means walking that list, one step per key. A rule that turns a key into a slot is called a hash.
claims.source: Collision resolution by chaining: Cormen et al., Introduction to Algorithms (3rd ed.), 11.2; search time is proportional to the chain length.

claims.text: A good hash breaks up the patterns real keys have, such as all ending in 0; the table size was not the problem here.
claims.source: CLRS 11.3 (a good hash function should not depend on patterns in the keys; the division method avoids moduli like powers of 10 for decimal keys). The 'not the size' part follows from c1: 10 slots for 10 keys.

claims.text: 23 mod 10 is 3, so key 23 goes in slot 3.

recall.question: A shop's prices are all whole dollars ending in 5 or 0 (5, 10, 15, ...). It hashes them with slot = price mod 10 into 10 slots. What goes wrong?
options: They all land in just 2 slots
Every price gets its own slot
recall.why: Prices ending in 5 or 0 leave remainder 5 or 0, so the rule uses only 2 of 10 slots: the pattern in the keys survives a weak hash.
